title: implement-now — plan 001
epic_title: Build the pyxis-native local execution engine (/implement-now)

tasks.title: Define the five ports and the single-task Worker cycle
tasks.goal: A single-task Worker runs the whole cycle — claim → workspace → run agent → open+verify proposal → release — end to end against inline fakes, hermetically.
tasks.current: No executor exists; pyxis plans and projects but has no code that turns a claimed task into a verified proposal.
tasks.desired: Given one task charter + repo access, the Worker claims, prepares a workspace, invokes the runtime, opens a proposal, verifies success by artifact (a proposal exists and is green — else `hollow`, never succeeded), and releases; it reads no sibling or session state.
scope: The five consumer-side port interfaces (WorkTracker, Lease, Workspace, AgentRuntime, CodeHost) as the engine's declared contracts.
The Worker composition of those ports into the one-task cycle, with hollow detection at verify.
Inline test fakes for all five ports proving the cycle in-process.
out_of_scope: Any real adapter (git, gh, or a CLI) — those are their own tasks.
Concurrency and the frontier walk — the Dispatcher's task.
acceptance: Driving the Worker with inline fakes runs claim→workspace→run→verify→release for one task and returns `succeeded`.
A fake run that produces no proposal is reported `hollow`, never `succeeded`.
The Worker reads only its one task charter — a test asserting no sibling/session state is consulted passes.
key_interfaces: `WorkTracker`, `Lease`, `Workspace`, `AgentRuntime`, `CodeHost` port interfaces; `Worker` with a `Run(ctx, charter)` contract returning a typed outcome.

tasks.title: The Dispatcher and the frontier-sweep run model
tasks.goal: One run computes the ready frontier over the frozen plan's DAG, dispatches Workers claim-serially then run-in-parallel, and ends with a classed report of succeeded, failed, and blocked tasks — consuming zero model cost when the frontier is empty.
tasks.current: The Worker (T1) runs one task; nothing walks the plan's DAG or bounds concurrency.
tasks.desired: The Dispatcher reads open∧unblocked∧unclaimed tasks through one predicate, claims up to the parallel-width bound one at a time (no two Workers per task), runs the claimed Workers concurrently, and reports each task's terminal class; an empty frontier reports and exits before any model call; one task's failure never halts the run.
scope: The single frontier predicate (open ∧ unblocked ∧ unclaimed) over the DAG.
Claim-serially / run-concurrently scheduling to a parallel-width bound.
The classed run report (succeeded / failed / blocked) and the empty-frontier zero-cost exit.
out_of_scope: Real tracker/runtime adapters (uses the T1 fakes/ports).
Turn caps, CI self-heal, and resume — later robustness tasks.
acceptance: A fixture plan with a foundation task and two file-disjoint leaves runs the foundation, then both leaves, and reports 3 succeeded.
A run whose frontier is empty emits zero model calls and reports nothing-ready.
With one leaf failing, the other independent leaf still completes and the report classes every task.
key_interfaces: `Dispatcher` with a `Sweep(ctx, plan)` contract; the frontier predicate; the `RunReport` shape.

tasks.title: Workspace adapter: worktree isolation off freshly-fetched mainline
tasks.goal: Each task gets an isolated git worktree branched off the freshly-fetched mainline, with the parent checkout mechanically protected from mutation and worktrees reaped when done.
tasks.current: The Workspace port exists (T1) with only a temp-dir fake; no real git isolation.
tasks.desired: Preparing a task fetches the mainline and creates a per-task worktree on a fresh branch off that tip; any attempt to mutate the parent clone is blocked by a guard; a completed (merged ∧ closed) or aged worktree is reaped; a task is never based off an unmerged blocker's branch.
scope: Worktree creation per task, branched off the freshly-fetched mainline tip.
A mechanical guard blocking mutation of the parent checkout.
Worktree reaping on completion or age.
out_of_scope: Claim coordination (the Lease adapter's task).
Any stacked-branch base selection — the base is always fetched mainline.
acceptance: A Worker's writes appear only in its worktree; a parent-checkout mutation attempt is blocked.
A dependent task's worktree is based off freshly-fetched mainline, never an unmerged blocker branch; no stacked PR is created.
A worktree for a merged-and-closed task is reaped.
key_interfaces: The `Workspace` port's git adapter; a worktree prepare/reap contract; the parent-guard.
touches: internal/executor/workspace (git worktree adapter + parent guard + reaper)

tasks.title: Lease adapter: the git-ref CAS claim shared with the fleet
tasks.goal: At most one Worker anywhere holds a task, via the same git-ref compare-and-swap the external fleet uses, plus a local in-process guard — every claim released on every terminal path.
tasks.current: The Lease port exists (T1) with an in-memory fake; no cross-process claim.
tasks.desired: Acquiring a claim is a create-or-fail git-ref CAS keyed by (repo, task); a local in-process guard prevents two local Workers racing before the CAS; a losing racer skips with no error; every terminal outcome releases the claim (fire-or-release); the executor coexists with the external fleet with no double-grab.
scope: The git-ref CAS acquire-or-skip claim, keyed by (repo, task), with holder identity.
A local in-process guard against intra-run double-grab.
Structural release on every terminal path.
out_of_scope: Cross-machine heartbeat/lease-expiry reaping (fleet concern, not the local runtime).
Workspace isolation (its own task).
acceptance: In a concurrent local+fleet claim race on one task, exactly one Worker ever holds it; the loser skips.
Every terminal outcome (success, failure, crash-path) leaves no claim held.
A lost race returns a distinct skip, never a hard error.
key_interfaces: The `Lease` port's git-ref adapter; an acquire/release contract with holder identity; the in-proc guard.

tasks.title: gh adapters: WorkTracker frontier/claim/verify + CodeHost proposal/checks
tasks.goal: Real GitHub adapters read the ready frontier and item tags, mark claims and comment, open a proposal from a task's head branch, and read its required-check states — all via exact, fresh reads.
tasks.current: WorkTracker and CodeHost ports exist (T1) with fakes; nothing talks to GitHub.
tasks.desired: The WorkTracker gh adapter enumerates open tagged items, verifies an item's automated-implementation tag, and comments; the CodeHost gh adapter opens a PR from the exact head branch and reads required-check states through the Checks API; every decision-critical read is exact and fresh (never a search index or cacheable conditional GET); the plan-new projection contract is consumed unchanged.
scope: The WorkTracker gh adapter: frontier read, tag verify, claim-mark, comment.
The CodeHost gh adapter: open a proposal from the head branch, read required-check states via the Checks API.
Exact/fresh reads for every consequential lookup.
out_of_scope: The claim CAS mechanism (the Lease adapter's task).
The CI self-heal loop (the drive-to-green task).
acceptance: The WorkTracker adapter returns exactly the open, automated-implementation-tagged items for a fixture repo state.
The CodeHost adapter opens a proposal from the exact head branch and reports its required-check states.
A stale-read fixture proves consequential reads use the fresh path, not a cache.
key_interfaces: The `WorkTracker` and `CodeHost` gh adapters; the Checks-API read contract; the automated-implementation tag.

tasks.title: AgentRuntime contract and the Claude adapter
tasks.goal: A fresh headless Claude process implements a task from an inline brief in its worktree, its completion read from the process exit and its token/cost parsed from JSON — behind the one runtime contract, with a conformance harness other adapters reuse.
tasks.current: The AgentRuntime port exists (T1) as an interface with a fake.
tasks.desired: `launch` spawns a fresh non-interactive process per task (no session reuse) with the full charter + relevant context inline; `await` reads completion from the exit code; the adapter parses the CLI's JSON for tokens/turns; `authcheck` preflights install+auth and degrades loudly with a stated remedy on a missing credential, consuming no attempt; `tiermap` maps the frozen rung to (model, effort) with native IDs kept inside the adapter; a self-registration registry (no central switch) admits adapters.
scope: The runtime contract (`launch`/`await`/`kill`/`authcheck`/`tiermap`) with exit-code completion and JSON token parsing.
The Claude adapter, self-registered, spawning a fresh headless process with the inline brief.
The auth preflight + loud degrade; a reusable adapter conformance harness.
out_of_scope: The other three CLI adapters (their own tasks).
Turn caps and the CI self-heal loop (later tasks).
acceptance: The Claude adapter drives a fixture task to a green proposal through the runtime contract, with a fresh process (no reuse).
A missing/unauthenticated backend degrades loudly with a stated remedy and spawns no counted Worker.
Parsed token/turn usage is reported for a completed run.
key_interfaces: The `AgentRuntime` contract; the self-registration registry; the ephemeral brief assembly; the Claude adapter + conformance harness.
touches: internal/executor/runtime (the contract + registry + brief + authcheck + runtime_test.go)

tasks.title: Codex AgentRuntime adapter
tasks.goal: A fresh headless Codex process (`codex exec`) implements a task through the one runtime contract, self-registered, passing the adapter conformance test.
tasks.current: The runtime contract + registry + conformance harness exist (T6); no Codex adapter.
tasks.desired: The Codex adapter runs `codex exec` non-interactively with approval/sandbox bypass, reads completion from exit, parses its JSON for usage, and self-registers; it passes the same conformance test the other adapters do.
scope: The Codex adapter: headless `exec` launch, exit-code completion, JSON usage parse, `tiermap`.
Self-registration (no central switch).
out_of_scope: The runtime contract itself (T6).
Routing which task uses Codex (the config task).
acceptance: The Codex adapter drives a fixture task to a green proposal through the runtime contract.
The adapter self-registers and passes the shared conformance test.

tasks.title: Cursor AgentRuntime adapter (under a pty)
tasks.goal: A fresh headless Cursor process (`cursor-agent -p` under a pseudo-terminal) implements a task through the one runtime contract, self-registered, passing conformance.
tasks.current: The runtime contract + registry + conformance harness exist (T6); no Cursor adapter.
tasks.desired: The Cursor adapter runs `cursor-agent -p --output-format json --force` inside a pseudo-terminal (the CLI requires a TTY), reads completion from exit, parses JSON usage, and self-registers; it passes the shared conformance test.
scope: The Cursor adapter: headless print-mode launch wrapped in a pty, autonomy flag, exit-code completion, JSON usage parse, `tiermap`.
Self-registration.
out_of_scope: The runtime contract (T6).
Backend routing (the config task).
acceptance: The Cursor adapter drives a fixture task to a green proposal through the runtime contract, running under a pty.
The adapter self-registers and passes the shared conformance test.
key_interfaces: The Cursor `AgentRuntime` adapter; the pty wrapper; its `tiermap`.

tasks.title: OpenCode AgentRuntime adapter
tasks.goal: A fresh headless OpenCode process (`opencode run`) implements a task through the one runtime contract, self-registered, passing conformance.
tasks.current: The runtime contract + registry + conformance harness exist (T6); no OpenCode adapter, and OpenCode is not installed on the authoring machine.
tasks.desired: The OpenCode adapter runs `opencode run --format json` non-interactively, reads completion from exit, parses JSON usage, uses `provider/model` naming in `tiermap`, and self-registers; the exact current headless flags are confirmed at implementation and locked by the conformance test.
scope: The OpenCode adapter: headless `run` launch, exit-code completion, JSON usage parse, `provider/model` `tiermap`.
Self-registration; flags confirmed against the live CLI at implementation.
out_of_scope: The runtime contract (T6).
Backend routing (the config task).
acceptance: The OpenCode adapter drives a fixture task to a green proposal through the runtime contract.
The adapter self-registers and passes the shared conformance test against the live CLI.

tasks.title: Drive-to-green: local gate mirrors CI + bounded CI self-heal
tasks.goal: A Worker drives its proposal to genuinely green — a local gate that runs the same checks required by CI, then a bounded self-heal loop that fixes remote-CI failures, capped, then escalates.
tasks.current: A Worker opens a proposal (T1/T5) but does not verify or repair its checks beyond a green/not-green read.
tasks.desired: Before push, a local gate runs the same deterministic checks required by CI (one predicate — a change failing a required CI check also fails locally); on a red proposal, a bounded state machine reads the Checks API, feeds redacted+clamped failed-CI logs to a fixer run, re-pushes, and re-checks, to a configured cap; at the cap it stops and escalates.
scope: The local gate that mirrors required CI (one shared predicate).
The bounded CI self-heal loop (read checks, redact+clamp logs to a fixer, re-push, re-check).
The cap-then-escalate terminal.
out_of_scope: The turn cap / checkpoint-resume of a single Worker run (its own task).
Merging or landing the green proposal (never in scope — the driver lands).
acceptance: A change that fails a required CI check also fails the local gate on the same input.
A red proposal is driven to green within the cap in a fixture, with failed-CI logs redacted before reaching the fixer.
At the self-heal cap, the task stops, is flagged failed, and escalates.
key_interfaces: The drive-to-green loop; the local-gate-mirrors-CI predicate; the bounded self-heal state machine.

tasks.title: Bounded execution and resume
tasks.goal: A Worker's turns are mechanically bounded and a non-converging Worker checkpoints, exits resumably, and is respawned up to a cap then escalated; a killed run resumes in-flight tasks from their pushed branches with no duplicate proposal.
tasks.current: Workers run unbounded (T1); the Dispatcher (T2) has no resume path.
tasks.desired: Each Worker's turns are capped by a native flag where present and a uniform wall-clock/budget cap + kill where absent; a Worker over the bound checkpoints and exits resumably; the Dispatcher respawns it up to a cap, then escalates; a re-invocation re-probes the tracker and continues in-flight tasks from their pushed branches, producing no duplicate proposal.
scope: Mechanical per-Worker turn bound (native flag or uniform wall-clock/budget + kill).
Checkpoint-exit + bounded respawn + escalate.
Crash/re-invocation resume from the tracker + pushed WIP, idempotent (no duplicates).
out_of_scope: The CI self-heal loop (its own task).
The in-session wake-driven auto-resume layer (a future design).
acceptance: A Worker exceeding the turn bound checkpoints, exits, is respawned up to the cap, then escalates.
A killed mid-run re-invocation resumes in-flight tasks from pushed branches with no duplicate proposal.
The turn bound holds uniformly across a native-flag backend and a wall-clock-enforced backend.
key_interfaces: The turn-bound enforcement; the checkpoint-exit + respawn contract; the resume-from-tracker probe.
touches: internal/executor/worker (checkpoint-exit + turn cap enforcement + worker resume_test)

tasks.title: Backend routing and the caps config
tasks.goal: Backend selection and the caps are closed-schema policy on the pyxis-config surface — a default backend plus an optional per-repo table, and the turn, self-heal, and parallel-width caps — with unknown keys erroring and enforcement mechanical.
tasks.current: Backends are self-registered (T6–T9) but nothing selects one per task; caps are hardcoded or absent.
tasks.desired: An executor config block carries a default backend plus an optional per-repo `(task type | phase) → backend` table, and the worker-turn / CI-self-heal / parallel-width caps, with sensible defaults + per-repo override; config parses closed (unknown keys error); the frozen rung is clamped to (model, effort) within the chosen backend; caps are enforced mechanically, never model-judged.
scope: The default-backend + per-repo routing table on the closed-schema config surface.
The three caps as config with defaults + override.
The downstream rung clamp to (model, effort).
out_of_scope: Per-task CLI override (deferred to a future plan-charter field).
The plan-time rung envelope (routing-envelope owns it).
acceptance: A repo config selects the default backend and a per-repo table routes a matching task to its backend.
An unknown config key is a parse error.
The caps read from config are enforced mechanically in a fixture.
key_interfaces: The executor config block schema; the routing lookup; the caps; the rung clamp.

tasks.title: The /implement-now surface and two-sink reporting
tasks.goal: The operator (attended) and argus (unattended) drive the same frontier-sweep through one normalized event stream — a live progress view in the session, or argus's delivery journal with fail-closed escalation — via the vendor-neutral `/implement-now` surface.
tasks.current: The Dispatcher runs a sweep (T2) but emits no normalized events and has no operator/argus surface.
tasks.desired: A run emits one normalized event stream (dispatched → verified → outcome → finished) delivered to two sinks: attended → a live in-session progress view + a classed final summary; unattended → argus's existing delivery journal, a stuck/failed task fail-closed-escalating to argus; intervention is coarse (cancel a run / kill a Worker); the surface is a vendor-neutral skill + authoring guide with a thin `cmd` main.
scope: The one normalized event stream and the two sinks (operator live view · argus journal + escalation).
The vendor-neutral `/implement-now` skill + authoring guide + thin main.
Coarse intervention (cancel/kill).
out_of_scope: The argus drive protocol itself (argus owns it; this feeds its journal).
Landing/merge (merge-lane's).
acceptance: The same run completes and reports under an attended invocation (live view) and an unattended (journal-only) invocation.
The event stream carries the per-task lifecycle events, and a stuck task escalates fail-closed to the argus sink.
Cancelling a run kills its in-flight Workers and releases their claims.
key_interfaces: The normalized event stream; the two sink adapters; the `/implement-now` skill + authoring guide + `cmd` main.
touches: the implement-now skill + authoring guide (the vendor-neutral agent surface)

tasks.title: End-to-end verification, dogfood, and the stage-8 map re-pin
tasks.goal: A real small pyxis feature is implemented end to end by `/implement-now` locally, the Worker core proves runtime-agnostic behind a second (fake/remote-shaped) Dispatcher adapter, and the pipeline map's stage-8 row states the native-local binding.
tasks.current: The engine's parts exist and are unit/conformance tested; no whole-system drill or map correction has run.
tasks.desired: An end-to-end drill runs a real frozen plan through `/implement-now` to green PRs (operator only reviewing/merging); the Worker core + ports pass conformance behind a fake Dispatcher adapter with zero Worker change (the reusability check); the pipeline map's stage-8 row is moved to state the native-local runtime binding alongside the external fleet.
scope: The end-to-end drill (a real plan → green PRs via `/implement-now`).
The reusability check (the Worker core behind a second Dispatcher adapter, no Worker change).
The pipeline-map stage-8 row correction.
out_of_scope: The remote/Docker Dispatcher binding itself (a future design).
Any PRD amendment content (the FR-10/FR-20 re-pin is a follow-up amendment, not this task).
acceptance: `/implement-now` implements one real small pyxis feature end to end locally, with the operator only reviewing/merging.
The Worker core passes conformance behind a second (fake/remote-shaped) Dispatcher adapter with no Worker change.
The pipeline map's stage-8 row states the native-local binding.
key_interfaces: The end-to-end drill; the second Dispatcher adapter (the reusability witness); the pipeline-map stage-8 row.
touches: the operational pipeline map's stage-8 row
